summary.intent: Execute Phase 19.2 (IPFS upload performance optimization), close verification gaps with matched local baselines, handle PR review cycles, and migrate staging IPFS datastore from flatfs to pebbleds.
summary.outcome: Phase 19.2 fully executed and verified (4/4 plans), PR #342 merged with SDK concurrent pin orchestration and pebbleds datastore config, staging successfully deployed with clean-slate pebbleds datastore, and learnings documented in a separate docs PR #343.

repo: SDK concurrent pins (`Promise.allSettled`) alone cause a regression at 50 clients (p95 +139%, throughput -26%) because they double simultaneous Kubo pin load on flatfs. Pebbleds is required to realize the benefit — the two optimizations are synergistic.
Load test secrets (`LOAD_TEST_SECRET`, `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET`) must be passed as inline shell env vars — vitest does not load dotenv, so `.env` values are ignored.
Throttle bypass requires both `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` env var (sent as `X-Throttle-Bypass` header) and `LOAD_TEST_SECRET` for test login. Only bypasses when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`.

DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL in `apps/api/.env` was pointing at mock-ipns-routing (localhost:3001) instead of someguy on 192.168.133.114:8190. Load tests should use someguy for staging-representative behavior.
Valid CIDs are tracked in two tables: `pinned_cids` (file content) and `folder_ipns` (where `latest_cid IS NOT NULL`). Everything on Kubo not in those tables is stale.
Staging had only 1 stale CID out of 31,255 pinned — prior cleanup was effective.
`ipfs-ds-convert` is archived and incompatible with modern Kubo. There is no in-place flatfs→pebbleds migration path. Clean slate or dag export/import are the only options.
The `tag-staging-release` GitHub Actions workflow (tag-staging.yml) handles staging tags properly — do not push staging tags manually.

code.finding: uploadFile uses Promise.allSettled for concurrent IPNS publish + folder metadata update. Batch publish failure emits typed `ipns:batchPublishFailed` event. totalFailed check requires null-safe access since mocks may return undefined.
Added `ipns:batchPublishFailed` typed event for batch publish failures, consistent with existing `share:reWrapFailed` pattern.
Shared test helpers file extracted from three test files. Contains createTestConfig and setupFolder. Object spread used to prevent aliasing; deterministic test data avoids timestamp nondeterminism.
batchPublishIpnsRecords mock must return `{ totalSucceeded, totalFailed }` shape — returning undefined caused runtime errors after the totalFailed check was added to client.ts.

workflow: Concurrency probe pattern: run load tests at 1/5/10/20/50/75/100 clients to find the knee before collecting baselines. 50 clients was the highest clean run; 75 started hitting auth token expiry timeouts.
Sequential `ipfs pin add` over bitswap is impractical for bulk CID migration (31K CIDs never progressed past 1 after several minutes). Parallel pinning or dag export/import would be required.
For staged Docker datastore migrations: stop API first to prevent new writes, query DB for valid CIDs, diff against pinned set, migrate only valid CIDs, then swap volumes.
GitHub Actions review threads resolved via GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation; replies via REST `pulls/:pr/comments` with `in_reply_to` as integer field.
Multiple API processes can accumulate across testing sessions. Check for zombie pnpm wrapper processes with `pgrep -a pnpm` and kill by PID, not just port.

Three-point local comparison (no opts / SDK only / SDK+infra) at matched client count is more informative than staging vs localhost comparison — eliminates confounding variables and isolates each optimization's contribution.

friction: Sequential bitswap pin migration (ipfs pin add per CID) was completely impractical — 31K CIDs, stuck after minutes. Wasted significant time before pivoting to clean slate.
ipfs-ds-convert is archived and incompatible with modern Kubo — no in-place datastore migration path exists, which wasn't known upfront.
SSH access required 1Password agent to be signed in; `op whoami` showed not signed in, blocking direct SSH tool use. Had to use `ssh` as a bash command via the user's terminal session.
Multiple duplicate API server processes accumulated during the session, causing port conflicts and a transient DB health check failure.
Load test vitest does not load dotenv — secrets must be passed inline, which was not documented and caused confusion.
Pre-optimization SDK checkout for Run 1 required git checkout from a specific commit hash; working directory being inside tests/load caused the checkout to silently fail until caught.
Background task notifications for already-captured results (100-client and 75-client probe failures) arrived late and added noise.
Push of staging tag was done prematurely without using the `tag-staging-release` workflow — required revert.
open_items: Load tests should handle 401s with token refresh — JWT tokens expire under long-running 75-client load tests causing auth failures. Todo filed: `2026-03-23-load-tests-should-handle-401s-with-token-refresh.md`
Investigate removal of mock-ipns-routing layer now that someguy is properly configured in the stack. Todo filed: `2026-03-23-investigate-removal-of-mock-ipns-routing-layer.md`
Staging IPFS content is now a clean slate — existing staged content was lost. Users will need to re-upload any staging test data.

SC3 (>15% throughput improvement at 50+ concurrent clients) was not met — actual result was +7% throughput. The tail latency improvements (p95 -13%, p99 -15%) are substantial but the throughput threshold was missed.

75-client bonus run with pebbleds shows dramatic improvement (p95 -53%, throughput +44%, errors eliminated) but was not captured as an official baseline — only documented in post-optimization-baselines.md.
Prometheus histogram verification on staging (human_needed item from VERIFICATION.md) is still pending — requires live staging Grafana access.
Production datastore migration strategy documented in `.learnings/2026-03-24-ipfs-datastore-migration.md` (PR #343) — dag export/import is the recommended approach when data preservation is required.
PR #342 merged but `console.warn` → injectable logger pattern across 5+ SDK call sites was noted as pre-existing tech debt, not addressed.
